title: Operators, precedence and formatted I/O
subtitle: Expressions are evaluated in a fixed order. Know it, and you can predict any line of arithmetic.

arith.title: Arithmetic operators
arith.body: + - * / and the remainder %. With two integers, / is integer division (truncates): 7/2 is 3, not 3.5; % gives the leftover: 7 % 3 is 1. To get 3.5 make one operand a double (7/2.0).

prec.title: Precedence and associativity
prec.body: From high to low: parentheses, unary (! - ++ --), * / %, + -, relational (< > <= >=), equality (== !=), &&, ||, assignment. Equal precedence goes left to right (assignment right to left). When unsure, add parentheses.
prec.steps: Evaluate 2 + 3 * 4 − 6 / 2. Multiplication and division first: 12 and 3. Then left to right.

incr.title: Increment, compound assignment, conversion
incr.body: x += 5 means x = x + 5. i++ uses i then adds 1; ++i adds 1 then uses it. In mixed expressions the smaller type is promoted (int → double). A cast forces it: (double)a / b.

logic.title: Relational, logical and bitwise
logic.body: In C, 0 is false and any non-zero is true; comparisons yield 0 or 1. && and || short-circuit: in a != 0 && x/a > 1 the division is never attempted when a is 0. Bitwise: & | ^ ~ << >> work on bits: x << 1 doubles an integer.

io.title: printf and scanf
io.body: printf("fmt", args) writes formatted output; conversion specifiers: %d int, %f double/float, %c char, %s string, %x hex; %5.2f means width 5, 2 decimals. scanf("%d", &n) reads input — note the &: scanf needs the variable’s address so it can store into it. getchar/putchar handle single characters.
